candidates.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation of a systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region, along with ECG findings of a complete right bundle-branch block and a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography, suggests a diagnosis of Atrial Septal Defect (ASD). The patient's age and lack of symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, or palpitations also support this diagnosis.

The patient's ECG findings and echocardiography results, which show a large defect with left-to-right shunt, could also be consistent with a diagnosis of Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD). However, the location of the murmur in the left upper parasternal region is more typical of ASD.
The patient's presentation could also be consistent with a Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO), although the size of the defect and the presence of a left-to-right shunt are more suggestive of ASD or VSD.

The patient's systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region could also be due to Pulmonary Stenosis, although the ECG findings and echocardiography results do not support this diagnosis as strongly as they do ASD or VSD.

The patient's ECG findings of a complete right bundle-branch block could also be seen in Ebstein's Anomaly, although the echocardiography results do not support this diagnosis as strongly as they do ASD or VSD.
